name: glycemic goals of care overview
title: Setting an A1c target in an adult with diabetes: if severe lows are unlikely, aim for 6.5% (low-risk type 2) or 7.0% (most people); if lows are likely or dangerous, or life is short, liberalize to 7.1-8.5% or stop measuring; each column gives who, why and what to do

nodes.title: Which A1c target? Weigh fewer complications against HYPOGLYCEMIA
lines: minimum for EVERY patient: free of symptomatic highs AND lows
decide WITH the patient: benefit vs lows, out-of-pocket cost, feasibility
A1c > 7%: microvascular AND cardiovascular risk ↑ · fasting and after-meal glucose both track risk

nodes.title: Severe lows UNLIKELY: prevent complications
lines: the more years ahead, the more there is to prevent

nodes.title: Lows LIKELY or DANGEROUS, or life SHORT: LIBERALIZE
lines: the main side effect of insulin and secretagogues is hypoglycemia

nodes.title: A1c ≤ 6.5%
lines: type 2 diabetes (T2DM) at LOW risk of hypoglycemia

nodes.title: A1c ≤ 7.0%
lines: MOST adults with type 1 (T1DM) or type 2 diabetes

nodes.title: A1c 7.1–8.5%
lines: functionally dependent: 7.1–8.0%

nodes.title: Limited life or end of life
lines: limited life expectancy: 7.1–8.5%
end of life: NO A1c

nodes.title: Young, short duration
lines: • long life expectancy
• no complications yet: still preventable
• not on a drug that causes lows

nodes.title: The default
lines: • long duration, on insulin, complications
• but no severe lows, not frail, not near the end of life

nodes.title: Severe lows LIKELY
lines: • recurrent severe lows
• hypoglycemia unawareness

nodes.title: Lows DANGEROUS
lines: • dementia, seizure disorder
• frail, prone to falls, dependent

nodes.title: Life expectancy < ~2 years
lines: or end of life

nodes.title: Further ↓ chronic kidney disease (CKD) and retinopathy
↓ microvascular complications
lines: cardiovascular too, if started EARLY

nodes.title: A1c 6.0%: harm in some
lines: older, frail · long duration · advanced coronary disease · past severe lows

nodes.title: A SEVERE low can be fatal
lines: severe = needs someone else's help to treat

nodes.title: No time to gain
lines: the benefit on chronic complications is hard to justify against the risks

nodes.title: Tighten while lows stay unlikely
lines: case: 35 · T2DM 2 years · metformin alone · no complications
drug choice: see the GLUCOSE-LOWERING DRUGS tree

nodes.title: Self-monitored glucose (SMBG) targets
lines: • fasting 4.0–7.0 mmol/L
• 2 h after a meal 5.0–10.0 mmol/L

nodes.title: Over half never reach it
lines: ANY fall still counts (9.5 → 8.5%)
case: 52 · type 1 for 30 years, insulin · coronary disease, neuropathy · no severe lows

nodes.title: Liberalize + check glucose (SMBG)
lines: SMBG prevents, confirms and treats lows
case: 85 · severe dementia, dependent · on gliclazide

nodes.title: But NOT above 8.5%
lines: symptomatic highs + complications

nodes.title: Avoid symptomatic highs and ANY lows
lines: end of life: stop measuring the A1c

panels.title: The A1c: the best-validated marker, but it LAGS
items: mean glucose over the last 8–12 weeks, ~50% from the last 30 days: changes lag behind glucose, so SMBG guides medication changes
misleading with altered red-cell turnover or hemoglobin (iron or B12 deficiency, chronic renal failure, hemoglobinopathies, splenectomy) → follow glucose readings instead
SMBG frequency: individualize (type, drugs, control, literacy, lows, awareness, job, illness)

panels.title: Lows: glucose ≤ 4.0 on insulin or a secretagogue
items: no symptoms → think UNAWARENESS · mild: autonomic, self-treated
moderate: autonomic + neuroglycopenic, self-treated · SEVERE: needs someone's help
sweating, dizziness, fast heart, hunger · confusion, seizure, coma
highs (double digits): polyuria, nocturia, thirst, weight loss, fatigue → DKA, HHS
